BURSEVI:v10p314/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314/r7.claim: Pasture is the tender growth God brings forth for grazing animals, in varied colors; Ibn Abbas calls it green herbage.
BURSEVI:v10p314/r7.anchor: أي أنبت بكمال قدرته ما ترعاه الدواب غضا طريقا من بين أخضر

BURSEVI:v10p314/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p314/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains al-mar'a as green fodder.
BURSEVI:v10p314/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه ، المرعى الكلأ الأخضر

BURSEVI:v10p314/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314/r9.speaker: الجوهري
BURSEVI:v10p314/r9.claim: Al-Jawhari defines ghutha as flood-borne scraps and rubbish, and qumash as things collected from here and there.
BURSEVI:v10p314/r9.anchor: قال الجوهري الغثاء بالضم والمد ما يحمله السيل من القماش والقمش جمع الشيء

QASHANI:87:1-4/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:1-4/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:1-4/r4.claim: The pasture is worldly adornment, benefits, food, and drink, grazing for the animal soul and pasture for the powers that serve it.
QASHANI:87:1-4/r4.anchor: أي: زينة الحياة الدنيا ومنافعها ومآكلها ومشاربها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#2/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#2/r1.claim: Ibrahim glosses the pasture as girls or daughters.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#2/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم والذي اخرج المرعى قال : البنات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r5.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun before measuring and producing pasture highlights each attribute; فهدى then marks guidance as the effect of measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r5.anchor: وإعادة اسم الموصول في قوله : { والذي قدر } وقوله : { والذي أخرج المرعى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89/r1.claim: Al-marʿā is the grass that God causes to grow and that livestock graze.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89/r1.anchor: أي أنبت العشب وما ترعاه البهائم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r5.claim: The pasture comprises every kind of plant and crop.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r5.anchor: أي: من جميع صنوف النباتات والزروع، {فجعله غثاء أحوى}

KASHSHAF:87:4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:4/r1.claim: Akhraja al-marʿa means that God caused the pasture to grow.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r1.claim: A cited verse says pasture sprouts over the soil of ruins, with grief remaining in human hearts.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r1.anchor: وقد ينبت المرعى على دمن الثرى … وتبقى حزازات النفوس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r2.claim: The cited poem describes vegetation growing over the dust of ruins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r2.anchor: المرعى على دمن الثرى … وتبقى حزازات النفوس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#4/r1.claim: The pasture is what God caused to grow for animals to graze.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r4.claim: Al-marʿā means green vegetation and pasture, as the poet says pasture grows over buried soil.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والذي أخرج المرعى } أي النبات والكلأ الأخضر.

NAHHAS:v5p203/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r18.claim: Al-marʿā is coordinated in the genitive and means what grazing animals eat.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r18.anchor: في موضع خفض عطف والمرعى ما تأكله البهائم

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet loved this surah; Muslim reports that he recited it with al-Ghashiya at Eid and on Friday, sometimes reciting both on one day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] كان يحب هذه السورة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:4/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:4/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:4/r1.claim: After surveying vast existence, the surah completes its great glorification with an evocative image from plant life.

QUTB-ZILAL:87:4/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:4/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:4/r2.claim: Al-marʿa means all vegetation, broader than pasture for livestock; God apportions provisions on earth for every creature that walks, hides underground, or flies.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:4/r2.anchor: فهو هنا أشمل مما نعهده من مرعى أنعامنا

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r12.claim: After blessings particular to humans, the passage names a blessing for other creatures: God alone can bring forth pasture, not the idols.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r12.anchor: هو القادر على إنبات العشب لا الأصنام التي عبدتها الكفرة

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies pasture as green fodder, while the author's broader definition includes plants, fruits, crops, and grasses brought from the earth.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المرعى الكلأ الأخضر

STUDYQURAN:87:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:4/r1.claim: The pasture and its blackened stubble illustrate God’s power over the creation and destruction of living things; marʿā means all forms of vegetation.
STUDYQURAN:87:4/r1.anchor: These verses allude to the manner in which God maintains power over the creation and destruction of all living things

TAB-FULL:v24p313/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p313/r1.speaker: أبو رزين
TAB-FULL:v24p313/r1.claim: Abū Razīn glosses the pasture as vegetation.
TAB-FULL:v24p313/r1.anchor: عن أبي رزين، " {أخرج المرعى} [الأعلى: 4] قال النبات "

TAB-FULL:v24p313/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p313/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p313/r2.claim: Qatāda describes the plants as appearing in yellow, red, and white varieties.
TAB-FULL:v24p313/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {والذي أخرج المرعى} [الأعلى: 4] الآية، نبت كما رأيتم، بين أصفر وأحمر وأبيض "

ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r5.claim: Aḥwā is a circumstantial accusative modifying pasture: God brought it out green, tinged with dark hue, then dried it into brittle stubble like debris atop floodwater.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r5.anchor: أحوى أي أخرجه أخضر يضرب إلى الحوة، والحوة السواد.

THALABI:v10p183#2/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p183#2/r16.claim: Al-marʿā is vegetation in varied colors—green, yellow, red, and white—which God turns into dry, brittle matter; ahwā describes it black when dried and aged.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r16.anchor:
والذي أخرج المرعى النبات من بين أخضر وأصفر وأحمر وأبيض.
فجعله غثاء هشيما باليا

WAHIDI-QT:87:4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:4/r1.claim: The pasture means vegetation brought forth from the earth.

ELMALILI:87:4-5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r1.claim: The pasture is the grasslands and vegetation God brings forth for human and animal use, including plants, trees, and fruits, as 79:31–33 describes.
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r1.anchor: o otlaklar, o yaylalar, mezra‘alar, bahçeler, ormanlardaki türlü nebâtât

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.claim: The perfects are aspectual rather than inherently past; verses 4–5 show creation as ongoing world-sustaining activity through the pasture’s recurring growth and decay.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Dass Gottes Schöpfungstätigkeit hier nicht als einmaliger Akt, sondern als fortwährende, welterhaltende Aktivität verstanden wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:4:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:4:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:4:anmerkung/r1.claim: The wording parallels Q 79:31, where God brings its water and pasture out.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r5.claim: The verses may describe spring growth turning into black plant remains, or metaphorically living things receiving life and then dying.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r5.anchor: 4 ve 5. âyetler, Allah’ın baharda yeşil bitkileri bitirip vakti gelince onları kapkara bitki kalıntısı haline getirmesi şeklinde açıklandığı gibi mecazen

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#2/r1.claim: God brought forth the grazing growth that animals eat, fresh, moist, and green; the surviving source text breaks off mid-word after describing its flourishing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#2/r1.anchor: أي أنبت ما ترعاه الدواب غضا رطبا يرف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400#2/r1.claim: Al-marʿa is the grass God grows for grazing animals, in green, yellow, red, and white varieties.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400#2/r1.anchor: أنبت العشب وما ترعاه [النعم] (4) من بين أخضر وأصفر وأحمر وأبيض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r4.claim: With signs within the self already given, vegetation supplies the strongest horizon sign of resurrection: God brings out grazing plants through rain clouds, first and again.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r4.anchor: وكان النبات من آياتها أدل المخلوقات على البعث قال : { والذي أخرج }

BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r5.claim: The return of the dead is no harder for God than gathering and restoring plants after they break down into soil, so pasture demonstrates His power to resurrect.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r5.anchor: لأنه سبحانه وتعالى أقدر على جمع الأموات من الأرض بنفسه بعد أن تفتتوا

ALUSI:87:4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:4/r1.claim: God caused to grow the pasture that grazing animals feed on, fresh, tender, and verdant.
ALUSI:87:4/r1.anchor: أي أنبت ما ترعاه الدواب غضا رطبا يرف

ALUSI:87:5/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r11.claim: The successive descriptions imply gradual development, conveying nurturing as bringing something to completion little by little.
ALUSI:87:5/r11.anchor: وهذه الأوصاف على ما قيل يتضمن كل منها التدريج ففي الوصف بها تحقيق لمعنى التربية

BAGHAWI:87:4/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:4/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:4/r1.claim: God grows vegetation and pasture grasses for livestock, in shades of green, yellow, red, and white.
BAGHAWI:87:4/r1.anchor: أنبت العشب وما ترعاه النعم ، من بين أخضر وأصفر وأحمر وأبيض .

BAYDAWI:87:4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:4/r1.claim: God brought forth the pasture that grazing animals eat.
BAYDAWI:87:4/r1.anchor: والذي أخرج المرعى أنبت ما ترعاه الدواب

BIQAI:87:4/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:4/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:4/r1.claim: Biqāʿī moves from signs within the self to signs across the horizons, where vegetation is the clearest created sign of resurrection.
BIQAI:87:4/r1.anchor: ونبه بآيات النفس ، فلم يبق إلا آيات الآفاق ، وكان النبات من آياتها أدل المخلوقات على البعث

BIQAI:87:4/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:4/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:4/r2.claim: God brings forth pasture through rain from clouds, growing grass and other fodder for animals, both initially and again.
BIQAI:87:4/r2.anchor: بما أنزل من المعصرات فأنبت ما ترعاه الدواب من النجم وغيره بدءاً وإعادة

BIQAI:87:4/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:4/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:4/r3.claim: The annual restoration of pasture after it fragments into soil proves resurrection: God can gather the dead from earth even more readily than renew plants.
BIQAI:87:4/r3.anchor: أقدر على جمع الأموات من الأرض بنفسه بعد أن تفتتوا من الماء على جمعه للنبات الذي كان تفتت في الأرض وصار تراباً

DURR:87:4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:4/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR:87:4/r1.claim: Ibrahim glosses al-marʿā as vegetation or plants.
DURR:87:4/r1.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم عن إبراهيم { والذي أخرج المرعى } قال : النبات .

IBNASHUR:87:4/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:4/r1.claim: The verse recalls the creation of the whole plant kingdom, including trees, but mentions forage as one useful kind.
IBNASHUR:87:4/r1.anchor: تذكير لخلق جنس النبات من شجر وغيره

IBNASHUR:87:4/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:4/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:4/r2.claim: Bringing out the pasture means bringing it forth from the earth by making it grow.

IBNASHUR:87:4/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:4/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:4/r3.claim: Al-marʿā is vegetation grazed by livestock; it can be a place-name for grazing or a verbal noun used for the grazed object.
IBNASHUR:87:4/r3.anchor: الشيء المَرْعِيّ من إطلاق المصدر على المفعول

IBNASHUR:87:4/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:4/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:4/r4.claim: Choosing pasture rather than the general word plant evokes livestock’s benefit to people and preserves the verse ending.
IBNASHUR:87:4/r4.anchor: مادة الرعي من نفع الأنعام به ونفعها للناس

IBNATIYYA:87:4/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:4/r1.claim: Al-marʿā is vegetation, the basis of livelihood because it feeds livestock and some of it benefits people directly.
IBNATIYYA:87:4/r1.anchor: وهو أصل في قيام المعاش إذ هو غذاء الأنعام ومنه ما ينتفع به الناس في ذواتهم

IBNKATHIR:87:4/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:4/r1.claim: God brought forth every kind of plant and crop.

IBNKATHIR:87:5/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r3.claim: Some Arab-language scholars take the word order as postponed: God brought forth dark-green pasture, then made it debris.
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r3.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب{[29970]}  يرى أن ذلك من المؤخر الذي معناه التقديم

IBNKATHIR:87:5/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir rejects the possible inverted order because it conflicts with the exegetes’ transmitted explanations.
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r4.anchor: ثم قال ابن جرير : وهذا وإن كان محتملا إلا أنه غير صواب ؛ لمخالفته أقوال أهل التأويل

MAWARDI:87:4/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:4/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:4/r1.claim: Al-marʿā means vegetation because livestock graze on it; al-Māwardī cites a verse by Zafar ibn al-Ḥārith as evidence.
MAWARDI:87:4/r1.anchor: يعني النبات ،   لأن البهائم ترعاه ،   قال الشاعر

NASAFI:87:4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:4/r1.claim: God brought forth the pasture that animals graze.
NASAFI:87:4/r1.anchor: { والذى أَخْرَجَ المرعى } أنبت ما ترعاه الدواب

QURTUBI:87:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:4/r1.claim: Al-marʿā means vegetation and green forage; the cited verse uses it for pasture growing from soil.
QURTUBI:87:4/r1.anchor: والذي أخرج المرعى "  أي النبات والكلأ الأخضر

RAZI:87:4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:4/r1.claim: After mentioning blessings particular to people, God follows with blessings particular to other creatures.
RAZI:87:4/r1.anchor: لما بين ما يختص به الناس أتبعه بذكر ما يختص به غير الناس من النعم

RAZI:87:4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:4/r2.claim: God can bring forth grass; the idols worshipped by unbelievers cannot.
RAZI:87:4/r2.anchor: هو القادر على إنبات العشب لا الأصنام التي عبدتها الكفرة

RAZI:87:4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:4/r3.claim: Al-marʿā encompasses vegetation the earth produces, including fruits, crops, and grasses.
RAZI:87:4/r3.anchor: المرعى ما تخرجه الأرض من النبات ومن الثمار والزروع والحشيش

RAZI:87:4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:87:4/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses al-marʿā as green herbage.
RAZI:87:4/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المرعى الكلأ الأخضر

TAB:87:4/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:4/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:4/r1.claim: The pasture brought from the earth is fodder for livestock, comprising varied plants and kinds of grass.

TAB:87:4/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:4/r2.speaker: أبو رزين
TAB:87:4/r2.claim: Abu Razin explains al-marʿā as vegetation.

TAB:87:4/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:4/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:4/r3.claim: Qatada describes the growth as sprouts in the colors yellow, red, and white.
TAB:87:4/r3.anchor: نبت كما رأيتم ،   بين أصفر وأحمر وأبيض

BURHAN:v4p295/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p295/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p295/r3.claim: The sequence from bringing forth pasture to making it dark stubble also has intervening stages.
BURHAN:v4p295/r3.anchor: وكقوله ﴿ والذي أخرج المرعى فجعله غثاء أحوى ﴾ 4 فإن بين الإخراج والغثاء وسائط

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.claim: The preceding sūrah urges the Prophet to wait: persistent deniers receive only temporary respite under God's practice, and cannot escape His grasp.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.anchor: Sūrah al-Ṭāriq, the previous sūrah ended on urging the Prophet (sws) to show patience and to wait for the decision of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.claim: This sūrah shifts its primary address from stubborn Quraysh to the Prophet and, over at least ten following sūrahs, dispels his preaching fears in varied ways.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.anchor: while ignoring these stubborn elements from among the Quraysh, the Prophet (sws) is addressed directly and given glad tidings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.claim: Verses 1–5 direct the Prophet to glorify God, whose attributes show that creation and human physical and intellectual capacities mature gradually.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r1.claim: He rejects the common decay-based readings of black litter or waste: aḥwā describes reddish or greenish blackness produced by freshness, fertility, and luxuriant growth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r1.anchor: because of freshness, fertility and luxuriance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r3.claim: Through Imām al-Farāhī, the author cites Qaṭṭāmī's valley couplet depicting dense, layered undergrowth as evidence that ghuthāʾ can mean fertile luxuriant vegetation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r3.anchor: he wrote while praising a valley

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r1.claim: Because aḥwā does not denote decay-blackness and qualifies ghuthāʾ, the phrase means God brings out vegetation and makes it luxuriant and blackish green.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r1.anchor: makes them luxuriant and blackish green

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r1.claim: Al-marʿā is the growth animals graze on.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r1.anchor: أخرج المرعى } أنبت ما ترعاه الدواب.

DURR-FULL:v8p482/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r7.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r7.claim: Ibrahim glosses the pasture as vegetation.
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r7.anchor: عن إبراهيم {والذي أخرج المرعى} قال: النبات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r10.claim: Al-marʿa is vegetation, the basis of livelihood because livestock eat it and people also benefit from it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r10.anchor: والمرعى: النبات، وهو أصل في قيام المعاش

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r8.claim: Al-marʿā is pasture or herbage produced from the earth; its root also carries senses of guarding and tending.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r8.anchor: المرعى: أصله من الرعي وهو ما ما أخرج من الأرض، وهو الكلأ، ورعت الماشية الكلأ رعيا

MUQATIL:87:1-7/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r5.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r5.claim: God brings out winter herbage and pasture, then turns its fresh green growth dry and dark.
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r5.anchor: الذي أخرج الحشيش والكلأ في الشتاء، فتراه رطبا فيجعله بعد الرطوبة، والخضرة إلى اليبوسة

TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r2.claim: Al-marʿā is grazing fodder brought forth by God.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r2.anchor: المرعى ما ترعاه الدواب فالله تعالى هو الذي أخرجها أي أنبتها

TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r4.claim: Pasture growth and its change into dark dry refuse exemplify divine governance.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r4.anchor: وإخراج المرعى لتغذي الحيوان ثم جعله غثاء أحوى من مصاديق التدبير الربوبي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r4.claim: God brought forth plant life from the earth as pasture.
